meta.title: Aryan Sharma | Systems, AI, and Proof of Work

hero.headline: I build systems that turn messy ideas into working products.
hero.subheadline: My work sits at the intersection of AI, media, infrastructure, and product taste. I care about things that survive real production pressure, not just things that look impressive in a demo.

identity_trace.description: Aryan Sharma in cold outdoor light wearing winter layers and sunglasses.

identity.title: Not a template developer
identity.description: I do not like building things that only look finished. I like going deep into how a system behaves, where it breaks, how it recovers, and whether the final experience actually feels right to use.

case_files.title: Selected work
case_files.subtitle: Projects explained as systems, not just screenshots.
case_files.description: These are the builds that best show how I think: the problem, the machinery, the tradeoffs, the stack, and the kind of pressure the system was designed to handle.

projects.name: SEONE
projects.headline: AI-native media automation pipeline
projects.summary: SEONE turns long-form video into short-form, social-ready output through a proper pipeline instead of treating media automation like a single prompt and a loading bar.
projects.details: It connects download, transcription, analysis, rendering, queues, workers, storage, and final assets into one traceable workflow.
projects.problem: Long-form video workflows become slow and fragile when every step depends on manual editing, scattered tools, and no clear recovery path.

projects.name: CONTENT LAB
projects.headline: AI-native creative production system
projects.summary: Content Lab treats AI creative generation like a production system. It plans, follows brand constraints, checks output quality, and prepares assets for review and export.
projects.details: The goal is not just to generate images. The goal is controlled variation, consistent layouts, brand safety, and repeatable creative output.
projects.problem: AI-generated creative often falls apart when it has to follow a brand, maintain consistency across multiple pages, and move through a real review process.

proof_layer.title: How I judge systems
proof_layer.subtitle: The things I look for when production stops being polite.
proof_layer.description: These are the engineering habits I trust when a system needs to be reliable, explainable, and fixable.

principles.title: Idempotency
principles.description: Retries should not quietly create duplicate work or duplicate cost.

principles.title: Observability
principles.description: A system should leave enough evidence to explain what happened.

principles.title: Render parity
principles.description: The preview and final output should not feel like two different products.

principles.title: State machines
principles.description: Complex workflows need clear rules, not optimistic guessing.

principles.title: Golden threads
principles.description: Every job should be traceable from start to finish.

principles.title: Tests before code
principles.description: When correctness matters, prove the behavior before adding more implementation.

stack.title: Tools I work with
stack.subtitle: Grouped by the kind of problems they help me solve.
stack.description: I do not think of tools as badges. I think of them as surfaces for solving different kinds of system pressure.

philosophy.title: Operating principles
items: Build things that can be inspected.
Start from the problem, not the framework.
Make systems traceable, editable, and recoverable.
Use tests when guessing would be expensive.
Keep the clever parts backstage. Let the product feel simple.
Use cloud for leverage, but understand what it is doing.
Say what is true. Avoid fake certainty.

human_layer.title: Outside the work
human_layer.subtitle: Cold weather, blue light, quiet places, and systems that make chaos smaller.
human_layer.description: I am drawn to systems because they give shape to messy things. Outside work, I like the kind of spaces that feel quiet, slightly cinematic, and a little impossible.
